01Rationale

Why this level matters

AI assistants now write the code and the formulas. What they cannot do is know whether the answer is right for your business. This course builds the analyst's real skill: asking the question well, getting the data, and checking every result.

02Target competencies

Intended learning outcomes

Ask and answer

Turn a business question into data, a method and a clear finding.

Work with data

Use Python, SQL and Excel to clean, join, analyse and model data.

Show it

Build dashboards and reports in Power BI that people use.

Check the AI

Verify AI-written code and numbers before anyone relies on them.

04Planned practical work

An analysis you can defend

Proposed project: Take a business dataset from question to dashboard and written findings, with a log of how you checked the AI. This practical component will be developed and validated before the level opens.

The steps

  1. Write the business question
  2. Load and clean the data
  3. Query it with SQL
  4. Analyse and model it in Python or Excel
  5. Build the dashboard
  6. Write the findings and your verification log

Intended validation criteria

  • The question is stated before the analysis
  • Every AI-written step was independently checked
  • The findings state their limits

05How you learn

Proposed learning design

Worked examples

The professional academies begin with complete examples and make the reasoning behind good decisions visible.

Guided practice

Scaffolds fade as learners progress—from annotated examples to structured tasks and independent work.

Retrieval and review

Low-stakes questions prompt recall; review revisits important concepts. Model answers and rubrics make improvement specific.

Research-informed updates

The academies cite primary research and standards, record review dates and receive versioned updates as evidence changes.

The proposed learning design draws on retrieval practice, worked examples and spaced review; detailed learner materials will be published before release. Read the evidence and sources.

06Intended audience

What you need

No programming needed. Everyday spreadsheet use is helpful.
